title.en: Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Measures against Foreign Influence) Regulations 2026

completenessNote: 全文，共 34 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。附表 1 篇以 900000+ 序号随同收录。

text.en: 1. These Regulations are the Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Measures against Foreign Influence) Regulations 2026 and come into operation on 15 September 2026.

heading.en: Section 11(6) — governing bodies and responsible officers

text.en:
3.—(1) This regulation prescribes the governing bodies and responsible officers of entities that are not described in section 11(3), (4) or (5), for the purposes of section 11(6).
(2) For a sole proprietorship —
(a)the sole proprietor is the governing body; and
(b)the sole proprietor is the responsible officer.
(3) For an express trust —
(a)the trustees are the governing body; and
(b)every trustee is a responsible officer.
(4) For a mutual benefit organisation registered under the Mutual Benefit Organisations Act 1960 —
(a)the committee of the organisation, as mentioned in the definition of “officer” in section 2 of that Act, is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)the president, secretary and treasurer of the organisation;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.
(5) For a platform work association as defined by section 19 of the Platform Workers Act 2024 —
(a)the executive or committee of the platform work association, as mentioned in the definition of “officer” in section 19 of that Act, is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)the president, secretary and treasurer of the platform work association;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.
(6) For a society registered under section 2(1) of the Co‑operative Societies Act 1979 —
(a)the committee of management of the society, as defined by section 2(1) of that Act, is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)the chairperson, secretary and treasurer of the society;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.
(7) For a trade union as defined by section 2 of the Trade Unions Act 1940 —
(a)the executive or committee of the trade union, as mentioned in the definition of “officer” in section 2 of that Act, is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)the president, secretary and treasurer of the trade union;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.
(8) For a body corporate that is not described in paragraphs (2) to (7) —
(a)the board of directors or any similar body is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)any person holding the office of chairperson, managing director or company secretary of the body corporate or any position analogous to any of those offices in that body corporate;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.
(9) For an unincorporated body of persons that is not described in paragraphs (2) to (7) —
(a)the executive committee of the body or group of persons analogous to the executive committee is the governing body; and
(b)the following are the responsible officers:
(i)any person holding the office of president, secretary or treasurer of the unincorporated body of persons, or any position analogous to any of those offices in that body;
(ii)if an office mentioned in sub‑paragraph (i) is vacant — any person carrying out the duties of that office.

7.—(1) Representations by an entity (X) under section 16(2) must be made in accordance with this regulation.
(2) The representations must —
(a)be in writing;
(b)be in English;
(c)state the relevant facts and issues;
(d)state X’s reasons for objecting to the intended designation, including any alleged error of fact or law;
(e)state the arguments supporting each of those reasons; and
(f)be accompanied by all documents supporting those arguments.
(3) The representations must —
(a)state —
(i)the name and contact address of X; and
(ii)the name and contact address of X’s authorised representative;
(b)be signed and dated by X’s authorised representative; and
(c)be accompanied by a copy of the notice of the intention to designate X mentioned in section 16(1).
(4) The representations must be sent to the competent authority —
(a)by email to MHA_RFPD@mha.gov.sg; or
(b)by registered post addressed to the Registry of Foreign and Political Disclosures, ICA Services Centre, 2 Crawford Street, #05‑09, Singapore 207218.

8.—(1) An application by a designated entity (X) under section 17(1)(b) to cancel its designation must be made in accordance with this regulation.
(2) The application must —
(a)be in writing;
(b)be in English;
(c)state the relevant facts and issues;
(d)state X’s reasons for seeking to cancel its designation, including any alleged error of fact or law;
(e)state the arguments supporting each of those reasons; and
(f)be accompanied by all documents supporting those arguments.
(3) The application must —
(a)state —
(i)the name and contact address of X; and
(ii)the name and contact address of X’s authorised representative;
(b)be signed and dated by X’s authorised representative; and
(c)be accompanied by a copy of the notice under section 16(4) of the competent authority’s decision to designate X.
(4) The application must be sent to the competent authority —
(a)by email to MHA_RFPD@mha.gov.sg; or
(b)by registered post addressed to the Registry of Foreign and Political Disclosures, ICA Services Centre, 2 Crawford Street, #05-09, Singapore 207218.

heading.en: Section 18(1) — obligation to report reportable donations

text.en: 9. For each reporting period, a designated entity must submit a donations report of all reportable donations that it accepted during the reporting period.

10. The reporting period for a designated entity is —
(a)for the year in which the entity is designated — the period from the date the entity is designated to 31 December of that year (both dates inclusive); and
(b)for every subsequent year — 1 January to 31 December of that year (both dates inclusive).

11.—(1) A designated entity (X) must report any foreign donation or anonymous donation that it accepts unless otherwise provided in this regulation.
(2) X need not report —
(a)any foreign donation consisting of money that is less than $10,000 in value; and
(b)any anonymous donation consisting of money that is less than $10,000 in value.
(3) If X is not subject to any foreign influence restraining order during a reporting period, X need not report any non‑monetary donation it accepted during that period.
(4) If X is subject to a foreign influence restraining order at any time during a reporting period, X need not report any non‑monetary donation it accepted during that period that is less than $10,000 in value.

13.—(1) A donations report made by a designated entity (X) must include a signed declaration by every responsible officer of X.
(2) A declaration by a responsible officer of X under paragraph (1) must state that, to the best of his or her knowledge and belief, for the reporting period covered by the donations report, X did not accept any reportable donation that was not reported.

14.—(1) A donations report for a reporting period ending in a given year must be submitted to the competent authority on or before 1 April of the next year.
(2) However, a donations report for a reporting period that ends on 31 December 2026 must be submitted to the competent authority on or before 1 April 2028.

heading.en: Section 18(2)(f) — form and manner of submission

text.en:
15. A donations report must be —
(a)made using the appropriate form;
(b)completed in English; and
(c)submitted to the competent authority through the Internet website at https://eservices2.mha.gov.sg/rds.

heading.en: Section 19(1) — obligation to report foreign affiliations

text.en: 16. For each reporting period, a designated entity must submit a foreign affiliations report of all its foreign affiliations during that period, including any foreign affiliation that ended or was formed at any time during that period.

17. The reporting period for a designated entity is —
(a)for the year in which the entity is designated — the period from the date the entity is designated to 31 December of that year (both dates inclusive); and
(b)for every subsequent year —1 January to 31 December of that year (both dates inclusive).

19.—(1) A foreign affiliations report made by a designated entity (X) must include a signed declaration by every responsible officer of X.
(2) A declaration by a responsible officer of X under paragraph (1) must state that, to the best of his or her knowledge and belief, for the reporting period covered by the foreign affiliations report, X did not have any foreign affiliation that was not reported.

20.—(1) A foreign affiliations report for a reporting period ending in a given year must be submitted to the competent authority on or before 1 April of the next year.
(2) However, a foreign affiliations report for a reporting period that ends on 31 December 2026 must be submitted to the competent authority on or before 1 April 2028.

heading.en: Section 19(2)(f) — form and manner of submission

text.en:
21. A foreign affiliations report must be —
(a)made using the appropriate form;
(b)completed in English; and
(c)submitted to the competent authority through the Internet website at https://eservices2.mha.gov.sg/rds.

22.—(1) For the purposes of section 20, a designated entity (X) must submit a key management report in accordance with this regulation.
(2) The report must be submitted to the competent authority within 60 days after the date on which X is designated.
(3) The report must be accompanied by a copy of X’s constitutional documents as in force on the date on which X is designated.
(4) The report must state, for each individual who is a member of X’s governing body —
(a)the individual’s identity particulars;
(b)the individual’s contact address;
(c)the office (such as president or chairperson) held by the individual as a member of X’s governing body; and
(d)the date on which the individual assumed that office.
(5) The report must state, for each individual who is a responsible officer of X —
(a)the individual’s identity particulars;
(b)the individual’s contact address;
(c)the office held by the individual that makes him or her a responsible officer; and
(d)the date on which the individual assumed that office.
(6) The report must be signed by every individual who is a responsible officer of X on the date of the report.
(7) The report must be —
(a)made using the appropriate form;
(b)completed in English; and
(c)submitted to the competent authority through the Internet website at https://eservices2.mha.gov.sg/rds.

23.—(1) For the purposes of section 20, a designated entity (X) must submit key management reports in accordance with this regulation.
(2) X must submit a key management report if any of the following events takes effect:
(a)an individual becomes, or ceases to be, a member of X’s governing body;
(b)a change is made to X’s constitutional documents and the change affects the size or composition of X’s governing body.
(3) The report must be submitted to the competent authority within 30 days after the date on which the relevant event mentioned in paragraph (2) takes effect.
(4) The report must be accompanied by a copy of X’s constitutional documents as in force on the date on which the relevant event mentioned in paragraph (2) takes effect.
(5) The report must state the relevant particulars for each individual who is —
(a)the reason for making the report under paragraph (2)(a);
(b)a member of X’s governing body on the date on which the relevant event mentioned in paragraph (2) takes effect; or
(c)a responsible officer of X on the date on which the relevant event mentioned in paragraph (2) takes effect.
(6) For an individual mentioned in paragraph (5)(a) or (b), the relevant particulars are —
(a)the individual’s identity particulars;
(b)the individual’s contact address;
(c)the office (such as president or chairperson) held by the individual as a member of X’s governing body; and
(d)the date on which the individual assumed that office.
(7) For an individual mentioned in paragraph (5)(c), the relevant particulars are —
(a)the individual’s identity particulars;
(b)the individual’s contact address;
(c)the office held by the individual that makes him or her a responsible officer; and
(d)the date on which the individual assumed that office.
(8) The report must be signed by every individual who is a responsible officer of X on the date of the report.
(9) The report must be —
(a)made using the appropriate form;
(b)completed in English; and
(c)submitted to the competent authority through the Internet website at https://eservices2.mha.gov.sg/rds.

heading.en: Notification of non-compliance with sections 23 and 24

text.en:
24.—(1) A designated entity (X) must submit to the competent authority a written notice in the appropriate form if —
(a)the composition of the governing body of X ceases to comply with section 23(1) or (2); or
(b)a responsible officer of X ceases to comply with section 24(1).
(2) The notice must be submitted to the competent authority within 30 days after the date on which the relevant event in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurs.
25. An appeal against a removal direction must be made and determined in accordance with the Schedule.

chapter.en: PART 6 REPORTING OFFENCES, ETC., PRESCRIBED FOR SECTION 22

heading.en: Failure to submit report in accordance with requirements

text.en:
26.—(1) A person commits an offence if —
(a)the person is a responsible officer of a designated entity (X) at any time during a reporting period or the period described in regulation 22(2) or 23(3) (for a key management report); and
(b)X fails to submit —
(i)a donations report in accordance with regulation 9;
(ii)a foreign affiliations report in accordance with regulation 16; or
(iii)a key management report in accordance with regulation 22 or 23.
(2) An offence under paragraph (1) is a strict liability offence.
(3) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (1) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)to a fine not exceeding $2,000; and
(b)in the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine not exceeding $200 for every day or part of a day during which the offence continues after conviction.
(4) In proceedings for an offence under paragraph (1), it is a defence for the accused to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that the accused took all reasonable steps, and exercised all due diligence, to ensure that the relevant report was submitted in accordance with the relevant regulation.

chapter.en: PART 6 REPORTING OFFENCES, ETC., PRESCRIBED FOR SECTION 22

heading.en: Failure to submit notice of non-compliance in accordance with regulation 24

text.en:
27.—(1) A person commits an offence if —
(a)a designated entity (X) fails to give to the competent authority the written notice required under regulation 24 by the end of the period specified in that provision; and
(b)the person is a responsible officer of X at any time during that period.
(2) An offence under paragraph (1) is a strict liability offence.
(3) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (1) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)to a fine not exceeding $5,000; and
(b)in the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine not exceeding $500 for every day or part of a day during which the offence continues after conviction.
(4) In proceedings for an offence under paragraph (1), it is a defence for the accused to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that the accused took all reasonable steps, and exercised all due diligence, to ensure that the requirement to give the written notice under regulation 24 by the end of the period specified in that provision was complied with.

chapter.en: PART 6 REPORTING OFFENCES, ETC., PRESCRIBED FOR SECTION 22

heading.en: Submission of false or misleading report with knowledge

text.en:
28.—(1) A person commits an offence if —
(a)a designated entity (X) submits any of the following to the competent authority:
(i)a donations report;
(ii)a foreign affiliations report;
(iii)a key management report;
(b)the person knowingly —
(i)stated or included any matter in the report that is false or misleading in a material particular; or
(ii)omitted to state or include any matter without which the report is false or misleading in a material particular; and
(c)the person is a responsible officer of X when doing so.
(2) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (1) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)to a fine not exceeding $10,000; and
(b)in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, to a fine not exceeding $20,000.

chapter.en: PART 6 REPORTING OFFENCES, ETC., PRESCRIBED FOR SECTION 22

heading.en: Submission of false or misleading report

text.en:
29.—(1) A person commits an offence if —
(a)a designated entity (X) submits any of the following to the competent authority:
(i)a donations report;
(ii)a foreign affiliations report;
(iii)a key management report;
(b)the report —
(i)contains any matter that is false or misleading in a material particular; or
(ii)omits to state or include any matter without which the report is false or misleading in a material particular; and
(c)the person is a responsible officer of X when the report was submitted.
(2) An offence under paragraph (1) is a strict liability offence.
(3) A person who is guilty of an offence under paragraph (1) shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000.
(4) In proceedings for an offence under paragraph (1), it is a defence for the accused to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that the accused took all reasonable steps, and exercised all due diligence, to ensure that —
(a)the report did not contain any statement that was false or misleading in a material particular; or
(b)the report did not contain any omission that would have made the report false or misleading in a material particular.

heading.en: Section 27(3)(b) — return or disposal of donation of money or property

text.en:
30.—(1) For the purposes of section 27(3)(b), a designated entity (X) must return or dispose of a donation of money or property in accordance with this regulation.
(2) If the identity of the donor is known, X must return the donated money or property to the donor.
(3) If —
(a)the donation is an anonymous donation;
(b)the donation was transmitted by a person on behalf of the donor; and
(c)the identity of that person is known to X,
X must return the donated money or property to that person.
(4) If —
(a)the donation is an anonymous donation;
(b)the donation was transmitted by a person whose identity is not apparent; and
(c)the donor has, in connection with the donation, used any facility provided by an identifiable financial institution,
X must return the donated money or property to that financial institution.
(5) If —
(a)paragraphs (2), (3) and (4) do not apply;
(b)the person to whom the donation is to be returned under paragraph (2), (3) or (4), as the case may be —
(i) refuses to accept the return of the donation; or
(ii)cannot be contacted; or
(c)X has spent or dissipated the donation,
X must dispose of the donation by paying the competent authority a sum equivalent to the value of the donation.

heading.en: Section 27(3)(b) — return or disposal of donation of services

text.en:
31.—(1) For the purposes of section 27(3)(b), a designated entity (X) must return or dispose of a donation of services in accordance with this regulation.
(2) If the identity of the donor is known, X must return the donation by paying the donor a sum equivalent to the value of the donation.
(3) If —
(a)the donation is an anonymous donation;
(b)the service was performed by a person on behalf of the donor; and
(c)the identity of that person is known to X,
X must return the donation by paying that person a sum equivalent to the value of the donation.
(4) If —
(a)paragraphs (2) and (3) do not apply; or
(b)the person to whom the donation is to be returned under paragraph (2) or (3), as the case may be —
(i) refuses to accept the payment; or
(ii)cannot be contacted,
X must dispose of the donation by paying the competent authority a sum equivalent to the value of the donation.

32.—(1) The competent authority may direct X to obtain an independent valuation of any property or service to determine the sum to be paid under regulation 30(5) or 31(4).
(2) The cost of an independent valuation may be deducted from the sum to be paid to the competent authority under regulation 30(5) or 31(4).
(3) All payments received by the competent authority under regulation 30(5) or 31(4) must be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

heading.en: Section 32(2)(b) — form and manner of application for exemption

text.en:
33.—(1) An application by a designated entity (X) for an exemption under section 32(1) must comply with this regulation.
(2) The application must state —
(a)the name and contact address of X;
(b)the name and contact address of X’s authorised representative;
(c)a list of every provision from which the designated entity seeks to be exempted; and
(d)the grounds for seeking the exemption.
(3) The application must be signed and dated by X’s authorised representative.
(4) The application must be accompanied by all documents supporting the grounds for seeking the exemption.

THE SCHEDULE
Regulation 25
Appeals against removal directions
Part 1
General
Definitions
1. In this Schedule —
“appeal” means an appeal to the Minister against a removal direction under section 25(3);
“appellant” means any of the following persons who makes an appeal:
(a)a designated entity directed under section 23(3) to comply with section 23(1) or (2);
(b)a person directed to be removed as a responsible officer of a designated entity under section 24(2);
“file” means to file with the secretary;
“party”, in relation to an appeal, means an appellant or the competent authority;
“reply” means a reply made by an appellant to a response;
“response” means a response made by the competent authority to a notice of appeal;
“secretary” means the Appeals Secretary appointed under paragraph 3(1).
How to file
2. Any document to be filed under this Schedule must —
(a)be addressed to the “Appeals Secretary”; and
(b)be sent —
(i)by email to MHA_PDD_RRP@mha.gov.sg; or
(ii)by registered post to the MHA PDD, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Phoenix Park, 28 Irrawaddy Road, Singapore 329560.
Appeals Secretary
3.—(1) The Minister may appoint a public officer to be the Appeals Secretary.
(2) The Appeals Secretary is to —
(a)provide administrative and secretarial support to the Minister in relation to every appeal;
(b)send a copy of any document filed by a party to the Minister and to the other party; and
(c)convey the decisions and directions of the Minister to the parties.
Part 2
Starting an appeal
Notice of appeal
4.—(1) A person who wishes to appeal against a removal direction must file a notice of appeal in accordance with this paragraph.
(2) A notice of appeal must be filed within 14 days after the removal direction is given to the designated entity.
(3) A notice of appeal must state —
(a)the relevant facts and issues;
(b)the appellant’s grounds for making the appeal, including any alleged error of fact or law; and
(c)the arguments supporting each of those grounds.
(4) A notice of appeal must —
(a)state —
(i)the name and contact address of the appellant; and
(ii)the name and contact address of the appellant’s authorised representative;
(b)be signed and dated by the appellant or the appellant’s authorised representative; and
(c)be accompanied by —
(i)a copy of the removal direction; and
(ii)any documents supporting the arguments mentioned in sub‑paragraph (3)(c).
(5) Except as permitted by the Minister, an appellant may not raise any ground that is not stated in its notice of appeal, during the hearing of the appeal.
Amendment of notice of appeal
5.—(1) A notice of appeal may be amended only if the Minister permits the appellant to do so.
(2) If the Minister grants permission to amend a notice of appeal, the Minister may also impose conditions and give further directions.
(3) The Minister must not grant permission to amend a notice of appeal to add a new ground of appeal unless the Minister is satisfied that —
(a)the ground is based on any matter of fact or law that came to light after the notice of appeal was filed;
(b)it was not practicable to include the ground in the notice of appeal when the notice of appeal was filed; or
(c)there are exceptional circumstances.
Withdrawal of appeal
6. An appellant may, at any time and with the Minister’s permission, withdraw a notice of appeal.
Summary dismissal of appeal
7.—(1) The Minister may summarily dismiss an appeal if either or both of the following apply:
(a)the Minister considers that the appellant is not entitled to appeal under section 25(3);
(b)the appellant has, without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with —
(i)the time delimited for the submission of any notice, document or other information in the appeal; or
(ii)any direction of the Minister in relation to the appeal.
(2) The Minister must, before summarily dismissing an appeal, give the appellant an opportunity to be heard.
Part 3
Response by competent authority
Competent authority’s response
8.—(1) The competent authority may respond to a notice of appeal by filing a response in accordance with this paragraph.
(2) A response must be filed within 5 working days after the competent authority receives a copy of the notice of appeal.
(3) A response must state the relevant facts and arguments that the competent authority will rely on in responding to each ground of appeal.
(4) A response must —
(a)cite the number assigned to the notice of appeal;
(b)state the competent authority’s contact address;
(c)be signed and dated by the competent authority; and
(d)be accompanied by any documents supporting the facts and arguments in the response.
No new matter to be raised in response
9.—(1) Except as permitted by the Minister, a response must not raise any new matter that was not contained in any material given by the competent authority to the appellant together with the removal direction.
(2) The Minister may disregard any new matter that is raised without the Minister’s permission.
Part 4
Reply from appellant
Appellant’s reply
10.—(1) An appellant may reply to a response by filing a reply in accordance with this paragraph.
(2) A reply must be filed within 5 working days after the appellant receives a copy of the response.
(3) A reply must state concisely the arguments in reply to the response.
(4) A reply must —
(a)be signed and dated by the appellant or the appellant’s authorised representative; and
(b)be accompanied by any documents supporting the arguments in the reply.
No new grounds to be raised in reply
11.—(1) Except as permitted by the Minister, a reply must not raise any new ground of objection against the removal direction.
(2) The Minister may disregard any new ground of objection that is raised without the Minister’s permission.
Part 5
DETERMINATION of appeal
Directions by Minister
12. The Minister may at any time give directions to the parties for the fair and efficient conduct of an appeal.
Powers to deal with appeal, etc.
13.—(1) For the purposes of determining an appeal, the Minister may summon any person in Singapore to —
(a)attend the hearing of the appeal; and
(b)do either or both of the following:
(i)answer any question under oath;
(ii)produce any document.
(2) A person who is summoned under sub-paragraph (1) commits an offence if —
(a)the person fails to comply with the summons; or
(b)in response to the summons, the person produces a document that —
(i)contains a material particular that is false or misleading; or
(ii)is false or misleading because a material particular is omitted.
(3) A person who is guilty of an offence under sub-paragraph (2) shall be liable on conviction —
(a)in relation to sub-paragraph (2)(a), to a fine not exceeding $2,000; and
(b)in relation to sub-paragraph (2)(b)(i) or (ii), to a fine not exceeding $5,000.
Hearing of appeal
14.—(1) The Minister must conduct a hearing of the appeal unless the Minister is of the view that the appeal may be decided based on the written or documentary evidence provided or produced.
(2) If the Minister conducts a hearing, the Minister must decide the date on which and the manner in which the hearing should be conducted.
Non-attendance of parties
15. If, at the time appointed for the hearing of an appeal, any party to the appeal does not appear, the Minister may, if satisfied that the party has been duly notified of the hearing —
(a)proceed with the hearing; and
(b)determine the appeal.
Interpretation and translation
16. The Minister may appoint any individual —
(a)to act as an interpreter in any hearing of an appeal; and
(b)to translate any documents produced in the hearing.
Rules of evidence not applicable
17. To avoid doubt, the Evidence Act 1893 and all other written laws relating to evidence do not apply to an appeal.
Representation
18.—(1) In a hearing, a party may be represented by any individual (called in this paragraph an authorised representative) who is allowed by the Minister to appear on behalf of that party.
(2) An authorised representative —
(a)may be an advocate and solicitor or a relevant legal officer within the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Legal Profession Act 1966; and
(b)must be a Singapore citizen.
Late filings
19. In considering any appeal, the Minister may disregard any document filed after the deadline imposed by this Schedule or a direction of the Minister for filing that document.
Decision of Minister to be notified, etc.
20. When the Minister decides an appeal, the secretary must without delay notify the parties of the Minister’s decision.
